subject.title: [Bug]: read tool drops memory/ prefix in multi-agent setup, causing ENOENT

question: Should OpenClaw accept https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96453's scoped read-tool ENOENT fallback for bare daily-memory filenames, or require the fix to move upstream to the prompt/startup path that loses `memory/`?
rationale: The bug is still present, but the candidate fix changes fallback semantics and the sandbox read boundary, so merge acceptance is a maintainer choice rather than a new automated issue fix.

options.title: Accept the scoped fallback
options.body: Land the linked PR if maintainers accept that missing bare `YYYY-MM-DD.md` reads can fall back to `memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md` after root-level ENOENT with guard coverage preserved.

options.title: Move the fix upstream
options.body: Ask for a replacement fix in the startup or prompt path if maintainers do not want generic read-tool date inference.

options.title: Keep waiting for different proof
options.body: Keep the issue open without landing the linked PR if maintainers want fresh Windows or live multi-agent proof before accepting either fix shape.

recommendation.title: Accept the scoped fallback
recommendation.body: Land the linked PR if maintainers accept that missing bare `YYYY-MM-DD.md` reads can fall back to `memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md` after root-level ENOENT with guard coverage preserved.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is centered on agent read-tool behavior and release/runtime safety, where recent adjacent history points to this owner path.
